added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: blocking: the map_worker claim loop keeps `handled: set[str]` (workers.py:791) keyed by source id alone and filters each IDS pass's claims with `sources = [s for s in sources if s["id"] not in handled]`, so a source claimed by an earlier IDS's pass is dropped from every later IDS's pass in the same run; a source with a selected MAPPING_CANDIDATE edge in magnetics and one in summary is mapped in magnetics only and never bound in summary, leaving its mapping_status at assigned. This contradicts the node's own docstring at workers.py:777-778 ('handled once by each IDS's pass') and §8's done-when ('the run's record of handled sources is keyed by IDS and source ... bound in both'). Reproduced by driving the real map_worker over target_ids_list=['magnetics','summary'] with one source carrying a selected edge in each: CLAIMS lists both IDSs but PREPARED holds only ('magnetics','magnetics/flux_loop') (log: repro_two_ids.log). The fix is to key the set on (ids_name, source_id) and to add the two-IDS map_worker test §8 names; TestMapWorkerMapsFromSelectedEdges (tests/ids/test_map_each_home.py:269) uses a single IDS and cannot catch this.

follow-on: `_mapping_status_for` is production-dead — it is exported only to tests, and the rule that actually runs lives in the reproduction Cypher in refresh_mapping_status (workers.py:381); TestMappingStatusSummary therefore proves a helper nobody calls rather than the status rule, and §8's done-when ('its Cypher is proven by a graph-marked test: a source with selected homes in magnetics and summary reads assigned with one bound and validated with both bound') has no test at head (no @pytest.mark.graph test references refresh_mapping_status or mapping_status). The two implementations can also drift: the Python helper and the Cypher each own a copy of the same rule.

item_verdicts.diff: read against base d8b537748; one commit, c4e3bf1b3, touching seven product files, three test files and the evidence fragment; the removed mapping_target_ids/mapping_target_path/mapping_target_type fields and claim_sources_for_assignment are gone with census grep printing nothing.
item_verdicts.done_when: most items hold at the head (section_of semantics, the assembler sibling-prefix fix, the section guard, target type from the section, the none-verdict leaving mapping_status unset, the progress cost line, the empty census), but two named items are unmet: map_worker maps a two-IDS source in only one IDS, and no graph-marked test proves the mapping_status rule (the tested helper is production-dead).
item_verdicts.goal: the node maps each IDS pass's selected sources from their selected MAPPING_CANDIDATE edges, guards each chosen target_id at section level (assembler.py:185 section_of comparison, mapping.py:1676 guard), derives the section and target type from the DD (mapping.py:270 _target_type_from_section), records a none verdict without touching mapping_status (workers.py:341 record_mapping_verdict), and refreshes the per-source summary (workers.py:381); but a source with selected homes in more than one IDS is mapped in only the first IDS, so the per-IDS goal is not met for the cross-IDS sources §8/§11 exist for.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, head c4e3bf1b3, gate exit 0 (2765 passed, 7 skipped, 2 deselected), negative_control.log shows the widened target_id guard failing TestSectionGuard::test_outside_every_selected_section_is_escalated; baseline_suite and after_suite read none: not an armed role, so the added-failure count is unmeasured.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares imas_codex/ids/workers.py, imas_codex/ids/mapping.py, imas_codex/ids/models.py, imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml, imas_codex/core/paths.py, imas_codex/ids/validation.py, imas_codex/ids/assembler.py, imas_codex/ids/progress.py, tests/core/, tests/ids/ and the evidence fragment; git diff --stat d8b537748..c4e3bf1b3 changes only paths inside that set and stages no generated model.

justifications.durability: the new tests cover section_of (tests/core/test_paths.py TestSectionOf), the section guard, target type from the section, the claim predicate, the assembler sibling-prefix fix, the progress cost line and the none-verdict; but nothing covers the run-level two-IDS claim-and-bind behaviour §8 requires, the tested _mapping_status_for (workers.py:368) is dead code the production Cypher does not call, and the mapping_status rule that runs (workers.py:381) has no test.
justifications.evidence: the broad gate is green (gate.log: 2765 passed, 7 skipped, 2 deselected, exit 0) and I re-ran the focused new tests at head to 103 passed exit 0; the negative control is genuine (it widens the guard and TestSectionGuard fails, EXIT=1); but the two behavioural proofs §8 names are absent — no test drives map_worker over two IDSs and no graph-marked test proves the mapping_status Cypher — and the passing tests test the pieces, which is why the multi-IDS defect survived.
justifications.fit: the change follows the repo's idioms — a Cypher status predicate beside the other claim predicates, a private _target_type_from_section beside build_target_assignments, section_of as the single path-section owner, and a separate record_mapping_verdict rather than overloading set_mapping_status; retired fields and options are removed decisively, and no plan, sprint or ticket label appears in a new symbol.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node wires the map stage to the selected candidate edges and derives section and type from the DD as §8 asks, but the claim loop's handled set (declared imas_codex/ids/workers.py:791, filtered at :805) is keyed by source id alone, so a source with selected homes in magnetics and summary is claimed by both passes yet mapped only in magnetics; the node's own docstring at workers.py:777-778 promises it is handled once by each IDS's pass, and §8's done-when requires the handled record be keyed by IDS and source.
justifications.reuse: section_of unifies the three copies §8 names (read_candidates' Cypher expression, validation.py's re-derivation, assembler.py's prefix test) — the plan's explicit ask, honoured; but the mapping_status rule is implemented twice, in the dead Python helper _mapping_status_for (workers.py:368) and again in refresh_mapping_status's Cypher (workers.py:381), against the plan's one-owner statement.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff --stat d8b53774..c4e3bf1b is inside the manifest's declared write paths; no generated model is staged; the retired fields are removed and grep -rnE 'mapping_target_ids|mapping_target_path|mapping_target_type|claim_sources_for_assignment' imas_codex/ tests/ prints nothing (exit 1).
